audit_findings.title: Pre-acquisition earnings are paired with post-acquisition units and debt
audit_findings.magnitude: 18.175323 million acquisition units, equal to 12.46% of the 145.892061 million fully diluted units; approximately $455.0 million cash consideration; June 2026 debt of $2.961 billion; J-W contributed $167.6 million revenue and $25.6 million net income from January 12 through June 30, 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: The post-close unit count dilutes per-unit value, while the pre-close OE anchor omits J-W earnings, acquisition-financing interest, corporate taxes and post-close maintenance capital. Debt is context-only in the bridge, but its interest expense belongs in equity-level OE.
audit_findings.evidence: On January 12, 2026, the Partnership and USA Compression Partners, LLC, a wholly owned subsidiary of the Partnership, completed the J-W Power Acquisition, pursuant to which USA Compression Partners, LLC purchased all of the issued and outstanding capital stock of J-W Energy from Westerman, Ltd. for aggregate consideration of approximately $860.0 million, subject to customary purchase price adjustments, consisting of (i) 18,175,323 common units representing limited partner interests in the Partnership and (ii) approximately $430.0 million in cash.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter mismatch, not merely a possibility. The valuation date follows the acquisition and the supplied rerun trigger, yet the numerator remains FY2025 legacy-company OE while the denominator is post-close. The share mismatch alone affects 12.46% of the denominator; omitted J-W earnings push value upward, while omitted financing, taxes and maintenance costs push it downward. The net effect cannot be determined without a consistent rerun, but it is reasonably capable of changing the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Rerun on one consistent perimeter: preferably post-close trailing/pro-forma OE using filed J-W results, acquisition interest, corporate taxes, normalized maintenance capital, purchase-accounting effects and the post-close fully diluted unit count; alternatively restore all inputs to the pre-acquisition perimeter.

audit_findings.title: Projected growth may double-count cash that must finance expansion
audit_findings.magnitude: At 16.2% RONTA, first-year investment implied by the $363.4 million anchor is approximately $112.2 million for 5% growth and $179.5 million for 8% growth; base versus bear value differs by $1.378 billion or $9.45 per unit, and bull versus bear by $2.398 billion or $16.44 per unit
audit_findings.mechanism: Growth requires expansion investment. Because available cash is distributed, externally funded investment creates incremental interest expense or additional units; either reduces equity OE per unit relative to a forecast with fixed financing claims.
audit_findings.evidence: Because we distribute all of our available cash, which excludes prudent operating reserves, we expect to fund any future expansion capital expenditures or acquisitions primarily with capital from external financing sources, such as borrowings under the Credit Agreement and issuances of debt and equity securities, including under the DRIP.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing establishes that expansion is expected to be externally financed, while the valuation compounds equity-level OE without an explicit financing cost or dilution schedule. The financing mix remains unresolved, but the valuation uplift attributed to growth is large and the investment implied by the stated RONTA is material. This omission is reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile annual growth to investment at the stated RONTA and rerun each scenario with an explicit funding schedule showing retained cash, new debt and its interest expense, or new units and resulting dilution.

audit_findings.title: Post-acquisition maintenance capital may exceed the anchor allowance
audit_findings.magnitude: 2026 filed budget of $60.0-$70.0 million versus FY2025 maintenance capital of $39.414 million, a $20.586-$30.586 million annual increase equal to 5.7%-8.4% of anchor OE; isolated base-case sensitivity is approximately $323-$480 million, or $2.22-$3.29 per unit
audit_findings.mechanism: Maintenance capital is deducted directly in OE. Using the legacy $39.414 million allowance for the enlarged fleet would overstate post-close annual and terminal OE.
audit_findings.evidence: We currently have budgeted between $60.0 million and $70.0 million in maintenance capital expenditures during 2026, including parts consumed from inventory.
audit_findings.explanation: The higher post-acquisition budget is demonstrated, although the normalized long-run amount is not yet established. First-half 2026 maintenance capital was already $26.177 million. The filed budget difference is large relative to the $363.4 million anchor and materially exceeds the narrow gap between market price and the stated buy-below price. Missing J-W earnings may offset some or all of it, but that requires a combined-perimeter rerun rather than ignoring the maintenance increase.
audit_findings.action: Use full-year 2026 actual maintenance capital when available and reconcile it to fleet size, age, utilization, overhaul cycles and inventory parts consumed; then rerun post-close OE and terminal value without netting against unverified acquisition synergies.

audit_findings.title: Unreserved IRS exposure is a potential senior cash claim
audit_findings.magnitude: The preliminary computation was $30.3 million and the FY2025 accrual was $2.9 million, leaving a computed preliminary difference of $27.4 million, or $0.19 per unit and 0.48% of the $5.711 billion base equity value; actual settlement amount unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: An unpaid or unrecorded settlement would reduce cash in the equity bridge or OE, but a payment or liability already recorded by June 30, 2026 is already within the latest balance-sheet perimeter.
audit_findings.evidence: The IRS has issued preliminary partnership examination changes, resulted in imputed underpayment computations of approximately $30.3 million, including interest, for the 2019 and 2020 tax years.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest 10-Q states that the IRS examination was settled and closed on April 13, 2026, that its impact is reflected in the financial statements, and that revised unitholder statements are unnecessary. The valuation uses the June 30, 2026 balance sheet, so the record no longer supports an additional unrecognized senior claim. Even the former preliminary unaccrued difference was less than 0.5% of base equity value.
audit_findings.action: Retain the settlement documentation in the workpapers and confirm that any cash payment or remaining payable is included in the June 2026 cash or liabilities; no valuation rerun is needed absent evidence of an omitted post-June obligation.

audit_findings.title: Affiliate expense allocations are uncapped and outside common-unitholder control
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed affiliate expense reimbursement was $4.6 million for FY2025 and $3.321 million for the first half of 2026; the latter annualizes to $6.642 million, approximately $2.042 million above FY2025 and 1.8% of anchor OE in total
audit_findings.mechanism: Affiliate reimbursements reduce operating OE; an increase above the historical amount embedded in the anchor would reduce forecast and terminal OE.
audit_findings.evidence: There is no cap on the amount that may be paid or reimbursed to the General Partner or its affiliates for compensation or expenses incurred on our behalf.
audit_findings.explanation: Historical allocations are already included in reported earnings, and the presently disclosed amounts are small relative to the $363.4 million OE anchor. The uncapped structure creates governance and forecasting risk, but a materially higher future allocation has not been demonstrated. It is therefore a forward-looking monitoring item rather than a presently open valuation error.
audit_findings.action: Track quarterly affiliate reimbursements, shared-services charges, J-W integration allocations and capitalized affiliate costs; rerun OE if the normalized annual expense becomes materially higher than the historical or first-half 2026 run rate.
